### Promulgate (ប្រកាសឱ្យប្រើ)

The Law on the Organization of Courts (ច្បាប់ ស្តីពីការរៀបចំអង្គការតុលាការ), which the National Assembly adopted on May 22, 2014, during the 2nd session of the 5th legislature, and which the Senate entirely reviewing the form and legal substance on June 12, 2014, during the 5th session of the 3rd legislature, and which was declared by the Constitutional Council to be in accordance with the Constitution in Decision No. 149/003/2014 KBTh.Ch dated July 02, 2014, and which has the entire text as follows:

# Law (ច្បាប់)
## On (ស្តីពី)
### Organization of Courts (ការរៀបចំអង្គការតុលាការ)

[IMAGE: Seal of the Ministry of Royal Palace]

# Chapter 1 (ជំពូកទី ១)
# General Provisions (បទប្បញ្ញត្តិទូទៅ)

**Article 1.- (មាត្រា ១.-)**
This Law aims to:
- Guarantee the independence of the judicial power (ធានាឯករាជ្យនៃអំណាចតុលាការ).
- Guarantee the impartiality (អនាគតិ) and protect the rights and freedoms of citizens.
- Guarantee the good functioning of the judicial organizations (អង្គការតុលាការ) and the prosecution organizations (អង្គការអយ្យការ).
- Promote public services to be efficient and fast.
- Guarantee the provision of justice in all types of cases to increase the confidence of citizens and contribute to strengthening social safety.

**Article 2.- (មាត្រា ២.-)**
This Law has the objective to:
- Define the organization and functioning of judicial organizations in all sectors and at all levels which are the adjudicating courts (សាលាជម្រះក្តី) of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
- Define the organization and functioning of the prosecution organizations (អង្គការអយ្យការ) attached to the adjudicating courts at all levels of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
- Define the jurisdiction (សមត្ថកិច្ច) of the courts in all sectors and at all levels according to specialization.
- Organize the management work, administrative work, and the functioning process of the courts.

**Article 3.- (មាត្រា ៣.-)**
The adjudicating courts (សាលាជម្រះក្តី) of the Kingdom of Cambodia include:
- First Instance Courts (សាលាដំបូង)
- Appeal Courts (សាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍)
- Supreme Court (តុលាការកំពូល).

The First Instance Court is the lower-level court (សាលាជម្រះក្តីជាន់ទាប). The Appeal Court and the Supreme Court are the higher-level courts (សាលាជម្រះក្តីជាន់ខ្ពស់).

Based on actual necessary needs, the establishment of any adjudicating court or other specialized adjudicating courts (សាលាជម្រះក្តីឯកទេស) shall be made by law.

**Article 4.- (មាត្រា ៤.-)**
Adjudicating courts in all sectors and at all levels implement the judicial power (អំណាចតុលាការ) covering all cases, including administrative cases (រឿងក្តីរដ្ឋបាល).

**Article 5.- (មាត្រា ៥.-)**
Lower-level adjudicating courts shall be divided into specialized courts (តុលាការជំនាញ). The establishment, abolition, and modification of specialized courts shall be defined by Royal Decree.

The President of the First Instance Court has direct administrative hierarchical power (អំណាចឋានានុក្រមផ្នែករដ្ឋបាល) over all presidents of specialized courts of that First Instance Court. Each president of a specialized court has direct administrative hierarchical power over the judges who are members. The President of the First Instance Court cannot serve as the president of any specialized court. Each president of a specialized court can serve as the president of only one specialized court of that First Instance Court.

Higher-level adjudicating courts shall be divided into specialized chambers (សភាជំនាញ). The establishment, abolition, and modification of specialized chambers shall be defined by Royal Decree.

The President of the higher-level adjudicating court has direct administrative hierarchical power over all presidents of specialized chambers of that higher-level adjudicating court. Each president of a specialized chamber has direct administrative hierarchical power over the judges who are members. The President of the higher-level adjudicating court cannot serve as the president of any specialized chamber. Each president of a specialized chamber can serve as the president of only one specialized chamber of that higher-level adjudicating court.

**Article 6.- (មាត្រា ៦.-)**
Only judges have the right to adjudicate (ជម្រះក្តី). Judges shall fulfill this duty independently (ឯករាជ្យ) while strictly respecting the law and to the best of their heart and conscience (សម្បជញ្ញៈ).

The adjudication of justice shall be done in the name of the Khmer people (ប្រជារាស្ត្រខ្មែរ) according to the procedures and laws in force.

Only the adjudicating courts have the power to judge and issue court decisions (សេចក្តីសម្រេច).

**Article 7.- (មាត្រា ៧.-)**
Hearings (សវនាការ) shall be conducted publicly, except where such publicity could cause danger to public order (សណ្តាប់ធ្នាប់សាធារណៈ) or good customs (ទំនៀមទម្លាប់ល្អ), or there are special provisions in the law stating otherwise.

In all cases, court judgments (សាលក្រម) and verdicts (សាលដីកា) shall be declared in the courtroom (សាលសវនាការ) which is open to the public.

Deliberations (ការពិភាក្សាសម្រេចសេចក្តី) of the chamber shall be kept secret (សម្ងាត់).

Unless there are provisions stating otherwise, the declaration of the court judgment or verdict shall be done by the presiding judge (ប្រធានអង្គជំនុំជម្រះ) or one judge among the judges who are the composition of the chamber.

Every court judgment and verdict must have reasoning (សំអាងហេតុ).

Unless there are provisions stating otherwise, judgments and verdicts shall be signed by the presiding judge and co-signed by the court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី) of the hearing.

**Article 8.- (មាត្រា ៨.-)**
Attached to the First Instance Court, there shall be a prosecution organization called the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court (អយ្យការអមសាលាដំបូង).

Attached to the Appeal Court, there shall be a prosecution organization called the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court (មហាអយ្យការអមសាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍).

Attached to the Supreme Court, there shall be a prosecution organization called the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court (មហាអយ្យការអមតុលាការកំពូល).

The representative of the prosecution organization must be present at every hearing of criminal cases (រឿងក្តីព្រហ្មទណ្ឌ) and other cases as defined by law.

**Article 9.- (មាត្រា ៩.-)**
In every judicial organization and prosecution organization at all levels, there are court clerks (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី) and administrative officers (មន្ត្រីរដ្ឋបាល), and there may be legal specialized officers (មន្ត្រីជំនាញផ្នែកច្បាប់) as assistants as necessary.

Court clerks assist judges and prosecutors at every stage of court and prosecution procedures.

The role and functions of court clerks shall be defined in the Statute of Court Clerks (លក្ខន្តិកៈក្រឡាបញ្ជី).

The modalities and conditions for the recruitment of legal specialized officers shall be defined by Sub-decree (អនុក្រឹត្យ).

**Article 10.- (មាត្រា ១០.-)**
At adjudicating courts of all levels, there is an administrative unit which is under the central administration of the Ministry of Justice to support the functioning of the judicial organizations and prosecution organizations.

At the level of the First Instance Court, this administrative unit is called the Administrative Secretariat of the First Instance Court (លេខាធិការដ្ឋានរដ្ឋបាលសាលាដំបូង), having a rank equal to a Department (នាយកដ្ឋាន).

At the level of the Appeal Court, this administrative unit is called the General Secretariat of Administration of the Appeal Court (អគ្គលេខាធិការដ្ឋានរដ្ឋបាលសាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍), having a rank equal to a General Department (អគ្គនាយកដ្ឋាន).

At the level of the Supreme Court, this administrative unit is called the General Secretariat of Administration of the Supreme Court (អគ្គលេខាធិការដ្ឋានរដ្ឋបាលតុលាការកំពូល), having a rank equal to a General Department (អគ្គនាយកដ្ឋាន).

**Article 11.- (មាត្រា ១១.-)**
The Ministry of Justice has the right to oversee the administrative affairs of all adjudicating courts, with a General Department of Court Administration (អគ្គនាយកដ្ឋានកិច្ចការរដ្ឋបាលតុលាការ) as the chief of staff. The Ministry of Justice may issue legal instruments (លិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្ត) and various necessary instructions to ensure the better functioning of court administrative management at all levels.

In case of necessity, the Minister of Justice may assign an inspection (អធិការកិច្ច) on any specific issue, and then report to the Supreme Council of Magistracy (ឧត្តមក្រុមប្រឹក្សានៃអង្គចៅក្រម) for review and decision.

Higher-level adjudicating courts have the jurisdiction to oversee the adjudication affairs (កិច្ចការជម្រះក្តី) of lower-level adjudicating courts. This oversight takes place within the framework of remedy procedures (នីតិវិធីឧបាស្រ័យ) in accordance with the provisions on procedures in force.

# Chapter 2 (ជំពូកទី ២)
# First Instance Courts and Prosecution Offices attached to First Instance Courts (សាលាដំបូង និងអយ្យការអមសាលាដំបូង)

## Section 1 (ផ្នែកទី ១)
## First Instance Courts (សាលាដំបូង)

### Sub-section 1 (អនុផ្នែកទី ១)
### Organization and Functioning of First Instance Courts (ការរៀបចំ និងការប្រព្រឹត្តទៅរបស់សាលាដំបូង)

**Article 12.- (មាត្រា ១២.-)**
The First Instance Court is the first-level adjudicating court which must be established in Phnom Penh and in every province of the Kingdom of Cambodia. Putting various First Instance Courts into operation shall be done by Royal Decree.

The First Instance Court shall be divided into specialized courts. The First Instance Court is a general adjudicating court (សាលាជម្រះក្តីទូទៅ) which has the jurisdiction to adjudicate all cases, except for cases which are under the jurisdiction of special adjudicating courts or extraordinary adjudicating courts (សាលាជម្រះក្តីវិសាមញ្ញ) established by separate laws.

The composition of the First Instance Court includes:
- President (ប្រធាន)
- Vice-president (អនុប្រធាន)
- Judge (ចៅក្រម).

- Vice-president (អនុប្រធាន)
- Judge (ចៅក្រម)
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី)
- Administrative officers (មន្ត្រីរដ្ឋបាល) and may have other legal specialized officers who work at the First Instance Court.

**Article 14.- (មាត្រា ១៤.-)**
Each First Instance Court is divided into specialized courts as follows:
- Civil Court (តុលាការរដ្ឋប្បវេណី)
- Criminal Court (តុលាការព្រហ្មទណ្ឌ)
- Commercial Court (តុលាការពាណិជ្ជកម្ម)
- Labour Court (តុលាការការងារ).

Other specialized courts of the First Instance Court may be established based on necessary needs. This establishment shall be done by Royal Decree.

Each specialized court of the First Instance Court issues its decisions autonomously (ស្វ័យភាព) within its jurisdiction in the name of the First Instance Court where that specialized court is located.

**Article 15.- (មាត្រា ១៥.-)**
The composition of each specialized court includes:
- President of the Court (ប្រធានតុលាការ)
- Judge (ចៅក្រម)
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី).

The president of each specialized court, including judges and court clerks, shall be appointed by the President of the First Instance Court. The process of these specialized courts shall be defined by the President of the First Instance Court in accordance with the legal instruments in force.

**Article 16.- (មាត្រា ១៦.-)**
Each specialized court of the First Instance Court adjudicates by a single judge (ចៅក្រមទោល) or by a trial chamber (ក្រុមប្រឹក្សាជំនុំជម្រះ) in accordance with the provisions on civil procedure, criminal procedure, or other provisions on procedures in force.

In case any judge has a task (ធុរៈ) or is in a situation of being unable to fulfill duties, that judge may be substituted by a judge in the subsequent order specified in the annual work allocation table of the President of the First Instance Court.

In case any specialized court cannot hold a hearing due to a lack of judges, the President of the First Instance Court shall appoint a judge from another specialized court to fulfill the requirement. If it is necessary to request one or more judges from other First Instance Courts to complete the composition of this specialized court, the President of the First Instance Court shall request the Minister of Justice.

**Article 17.- (មាត្រា ១៧.-)**
The President of the First Instance Court takes necessary management measures for the operation of the First Instance Court. In case the President of the First Instance Court is in a situation of being unable to work, or in case the position of the President of the First Instance Court is vacant, the Minister of Justice shall appoint a Vice-president of the First Instance Court, or if there is no Vice-president, may appoint any judge to serve as the Acting President (ប្រធានស្តីទី) instead to ensure the operation of the First Instance Court until the official appointment of the President of the First Instance Court. The appointment of the President of the First Instance Court shall be made in the shortest period and at most not exceeding 30 (thirty) days.

The President of the First Instance Court shall issue a decision (ដីកាសម្រេច) to:
- Appoint any Vice-president of the First Instance Court to manage the work on their behalf in case of necessity.
- Appoint a Vice-president of the First Instance Court to be in charge as the president of each specialized court based on skills or work experience. In case of a lack of Vice-presidents, the President of the First Instance Court may appoint any judge who has a high rank (ឋានន្តរស័ក្តិក) or extensive experience to be the president of a specialized court.
- Define the order for substituting judges in each specialized court and in the trial chambers of these specialized courts in case any judge is absent or has a task.
- Appoint and change court clerks in each specialized court according to actual necessary needs.

**Article 18.- (មាត្រា ១៨.-)**
In case of necessity, the Minister of Justice may decide to allow the First Instance Court to hold hearings outside its office location upon request from the President of the First Instance Court.

### Sub-section 2 (អនុផ្នែកទី ២)
### Jurisdiction (សមត្ថកិច្ច)

**Article 19.- (មាត្រា ១៩.-)**
The First Instance Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate cases within its territorial jurisdiction, except for cases where the law grants jurisdiction to other adjudicating courts.

In case of necessity, to guarantee public interest, safety, social security, and the good process of court justice, the Minister of Justice may decide to transfer the jurisdiction for handling cases from one First Instance Court to another.

In case of jurisdictional disputes (វិវាទសមត្ថកិច្ច) between various specialized courts within the First Instance Court, the President of the First Instance Court shall convene a meeting of the relevant presidents of specialized courts by their discretion or upon request from any president of a specialized court to decide on the jurisdiction. The President of the First Instance Court decides on this jurisdictional dispute by a decision (ដីកាសម្រេច). This decision is a final decision (សេចក្តីសម្រេចបិទផ្លូវតវ៉ា).

**Article 20.- (មាត្រា ២០.-)**
The Criminal Court of the First Instance Court adjudicates all criminal cases within its jurisdiction by implementing the provisions on criminal procedure, unless there are legal provisions stating otherwise.

The Criminal Court of the First Instance Court adjudicates criminal cases by a single judge or by a trial chamber in accordance with the provisions on criminal procedure.

The Investigation Chamber (មន្ទីរស៊ើបសួរ) of the First Instance Court is a part of the Criminal Court and has the jurisdiction to investigate criminal cases by implementing the provisions on criminal procedure. The President of the First Instance Court shall appoint at least 02 (two) judges by a decision to fulfill the role of investigating judges (ចៅក្រមស៊ើបសួរ) at the Investigation Chamber of the Criminal Court of the First Instance Court. This decision shall also define the numerical order for receiving work. In case there is no investigating judge or a lack of investigating judges, the President of the First Instance Court may appoint judges of other specialized courts to fulfill investigation functions.

In case of necessity, investigating judges may perform duties as judges at other specialized courts as appointed by the President of the First Instance Court.

**Article 21.- (មាត្រា ២១.-)**
The Civil Court of the First Instance Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate civil cases and all cases for which there is no provision granting jurisdiction to other specialized courts by implementing the provisions on civil procedure.

The Civil Court of the First Instance Court adjudicates civil cases by a single judge or by a trial chamber by implementing the provisions on civil procedure.

**Article 22.- (មាត្រា ២២.-)**
The Commercial Court of the First Instance Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate commercial cases, including bankruptcy cases (រឿងក្តីក្ស័យធន) in commercial matters by implementing the provisions on commercial procedure.

**Article 23.- (មាត្រា ២៣.-)**
The Commercial Court adjudicates with 03 (three) judges accompanied by 02 (two) advisors (ទីប្រឹក្សា) who are merchants or persons with knowledge of commercial law in the case of commercial cases where the object of the lawsuit has a value from 1,000,000,000 (one billion) Riels upward.

The Commercial Court adjudicates with 01 (one) judge accompanied by 02 (two) advisors who are merchants or persons with knowledge of commercial law in the case of commercial cases where the object of the lawsuit has a value from 100,000,000 (one hundred million) Riels to below 1,000,000,000 (one billion) Riels.

The Commercial Court adjudicates with 01 (one) judge without the need for participation from commercial advisors in the case of commercial cases where the object of the lawsuit has a value below 100,000,000 (one hundred million) Riels.

The judgment (សាលក្រម) of the Commercial Court shall be decided by 01 (one) judge or 03 (three) judges according to paragraphs 1 and 2 above after consulting with the commercial advisors.

Commercial advisors do not fulfill their duties permanently (អចិន្ត្រៃយ៍) in the Commercial Court of the First Instance Court. Commercial advisors shall come to fulfill their duties at the First Instance Court upon invitation from the President of the Commercial Court of the First Instance Court.

**Article 24.- (មាត្រា ២៤.-)**
The modalities of appointment and the fulfillment of duties of commercial advisors shall be defined by Sub-decree (អនុក្រឹត្យ) upon request from the Minister of Justice after consulting with the Minister of Commerce.

**Article 25.- (មាត្រា ២៥.-)**
The Labour Court of the First Instance Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate labour cases by implementing the provisions on labour procedure.

**Article 26.- (មាត្រា ២៦.-)**
The Labour Court of the First Instance Court shall adjudicate by 01 (one) judge accompanied by 02 (two) labour advisors (ទីប្រឹក្សាការងារ), one of whom is an employee (កម្មករនិយោជិត) and the other is an employer (និយោជក).

The judgment (សាលក្រម) of the Labour Court of the First Instance Court shall be decided by 01 (one) judge after consulting with the labour advisors.

Labour advisors do not fulfill their duties permanently in the Labour Court of the First Instance Court. Labour advisors shall participate in fulfilling their duties at the First Instance Court upon invitation from the President of the Labour Court.

**Article 27.- (មាត្រា ២៧.-)**
The competent Labour Court is the Labour Court of the First Instance Court at the place of the labour dispute (វិវាទការងារ).

Despite the definition of jurisdiction as in the above paragraph, the employee may file a complaint to the First Instance Court as defined below, unless there are provisions stating otherwise:
- At their residence (លំនៅឋាន) or
- At the location of the head office or primary place of business of the company or
- At the residence of the representative or person in charge of the company if there is no head office or primary place of business of the company.

**Article 28.- (មាត្រា ២៨.-)**
The modalities of election and the fulfillment of duties of labour advisors shall be defined by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice after consulting with the Minister in charge of the labour sector.

## Section 2 (ផ្នែកទី ២)
## Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court (អយ្យការអមសាលាដំបូង)

សមាសភាពអយ្យការអមសាលាដំបូង រួមមាន៖
- Prosecutor (ព្រះរាជអាជ្ញា)
- Deputy Prosecutor (ព្រះរាជអាជ្ញារង)
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី)
- Administrative officers (មន្ត្រីរដ្ឋបាល) and may have other legal specialized officers who work at the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court.

**Article 30.- (មាត្រា ៣០.-)**
The prosecution organization is an indivisible body (អង្គអវិភាគ). The prosecution has the function to conduct public action (បណ្តឹងអាជ្ញា) and request the implementation of the law before the investigation jurisdiction (យុត្តាធិការស៊ើបសួរ) and adjudication jurisdiction (យុត្តាធិការជំនុំជម្រះ), as well as implementing other functions as defined by laws and regulations in force.

The Prosecutor and Deputy Prosecutor are the representatives of the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court where they work. Deputy Prosecutors participate in implementing the functions of the prosecution under the leadership and collective responsibility (ទទួលខុសត្រូវរួម) of the Prosecutor of the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court.

In case of a task, illness, or absence, the Prosecutor shall appoint any Deputy Prosecutor to substitute. In case the Prosecutor is in a situation of being unable to work, or in case the position of Prosecutor is vacant, the Minister of Justice shall appoint any Deputy Prosecutor to serve as the Acting Prosecutor (ព្រះរាជអាជ្ញាស្តីទី) instead to ensure the operation of the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court until the official appointment of the Prosecutor.

**Article 31.- (មាត្រា ៣១.-)**
The Prosecutor has power over all Deputy Prosecutors within their jurisdiction. The Prosecutor appoints and allocates work to all Deputy Prosecutors.

The Prosecutor has the right to issue orders (អធិបញ្ញា) to Deputy Prosecutors to prosecute or to assign to prosecute or to make conclusions as they deem appropriate. The conclusions (សេចក្តីសន្នីដ្ឋាន) of the Deputy Prosecutor must be sent to the Prosecutor for review before the hearing. If the Prosecutor does not agree with that conclusion, and the representative of the prosecution who makes that conclusion still refuses to comply, the Prosecutor may appoint another Deputy Prosecutor or appoint themselves to be the representative of the prosecution in the hearing of the First Instance Court.

However, during the hearing, the Deputy Prosecutor may freely make oral observations (ការកត់សម្គាល់ដោយផ្ទាល់មាត់) according to what they deem to be in accordance with their conscience (សតិសម្បជញ្ញៈ). No disciplinary prosecution can be made against the representative of the prosecution because of their oral observations in the hearing being different from the written conclusions.

## ផ្នែកទី ៣
## Administrative Secretariat of the First Instance Court (លេខាធិការដ្ឋានរដ្ឋបាលសាលាដំបូង)

**Article 32.- (មាត្រា ៣២.-)**
The Administrative Secretariat of the First Instance Court is the chief of staff to the First Instance Court and the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court on:
- Personnel, administrative, and financial work.
- Court administrative management work for technical assistance to the work programs of the First Instance Court and the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court.
- Budget project preparation work for the President of the First Instance Court and the Prosecutor to review and decide.
- Regularly reporting on personnel, administrative, and financial work to the President of the First Instance Court and the Prosecutor.
- Implementing budget work according to the approved projects.
- Public relations work.
- Periodic submission of judgments (សាលក្រម) of the First Instance Court to the Ministry of Justice.
- Preparing and submitting monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual personnel, administrative, and financial work reports to the Ministry of Justice.
- Other work assigned by the President of the First Instance Court and the Prosecutor of the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court.
- Implementing other tasks as defined by legal instruments.

The Administrative Secretariat of the First Instance Court shall be divided into offices (ការិយាល័យ) according to actual necessary numbers. An office is led by one head (ប្រធាន) and several deputy heads (អនុប្រធាន) as necessary.

The organization and functioning of the Administrative Secretariat of the First Instance Court shall be defined by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice.

**Article 33.- (មាត្រា ៣៣.-)**
The Administrative Secretariat of the First Instance Court is led by one head and several deputy heads as necessary. The Head of the Secretariat shall be appointed by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice after consulting with the President of the First Instance Court and the Prosecutor of the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court.

The officials working at the Secretariat below the rank of the Head of the Secretariat shall be appointed by Prokas (ប្រកាស) of the Minister of Justice.

The Head and Deputy Head of the Secretariat shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 05 (five) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations. The Head and Deputy Head of offices shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 03 (three) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations.

All officials working at the Secretariat, including the Head of the Secretariat, must have their framework (ក្របខណ្ឌ) at the Ministry of Justice.

**Article 34.- (មាត្រា ៣៤.-)**
The general assembly (សន្និបាត) of the First Instance Court takes place under the presidency of the President of the First Instance Court and the Prosecutor of the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court to summarize past work results and define the administrative work direction of the First Instance Court for the following year. The general assembly report of the First Instance Court shall be sent to the Ministry of Justice.

# Chapter 3 (ជំពូកទី ៣)
# Appeal Courts and General Prosecution Offices attached to Appeal Courts (សាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍ និងមហាអយ្យការអមសាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍)

## Section 1 (ផ្នែកទី ១)
## Appeal Courts (សាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍)

### Sub-section 1 (អនុផ្នែកទី ១)
### Organization and Functioning of Appeal Courts (ការរៀបចំ និងការប្រព្រឹត្តទៅរបស់សាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍)

**Article 35.- (មាត្រា ៣៥.-)**
The Appeal Court is the second-level adjudicating court.

Appeal Courts include the Phnom Penh Appeal Court and Regional Appeal Courts (សាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍តំបន់). Putting each Regional Appeal Court into operation and defining the territorial jurisdiction of these Regional Appeal Courts shall be done by Royal Decree.

**Article 36.- (មាត្រា ៣៦.-)**
The composition of an Appeal Court includes:
- President (ប្រធាន)
- Vice-president (អនុប្រធាន)
- Judge (ចៅក្រម)
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី) and administrative officers (មន្ត្រីរដ្ឋបាល), and may have other legal specialized officers who work at the Appeal Court.

**Article 37.- (មាត្រា ៣៧.-)**
An Appeal Court has specialized chambers (សភាជំនាញ) as follows:
- Criminal Chamber (សភាព្រហ្មទណ្ឌ)
- Civil Chamber (សភារដ្ឋប្បវេណី)
- Investigation Chamber (សភាស៊ើបសួរ)
- Commercial Chamber (សភាពាណិជ្ជកម្ម)
- Labour Chamber (សភាការងារ).

In case of necessity, other specialized chambers of the Appeal Court may be established by Royal Decree.

Each chamber issues its decisions autonomously within its jurisdiction in the name of the Appeal Court where the chamber is located.

**Article 38.- (មាត្រា ៣៨.-)**
The composition of each chamber includes:
- President of the Chamber (ប្រធានសភា)
- Judge (ចៅក្រម) and
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី).

The president of each chamber shall be appointed by the President of the Appeal Court. The number of judges, court clerks, and the process of these chambers shall be defined by the President of the Appeal Court.

**Article 39.- (មាត្រា ៣៩.-)**
Each chamber of the Appeal Court adjudicates with 03 (three) judges, one of whom is the president, in accordance with the provisions on procedures in force.

In any case which the Supreme Court has remanded (បង្វិលមកវិញ), the Appeal Court shall adjudicate in a hearing which consists of 05 (five) judges, all of whom are judges who did not participate in adjudicating that case before, by implementing the provisions on procedures in force.

**Article 40.- (មាត្រា ៤០.-)**
The President of the Appeal Court takes necessary management measures for the operation of the Appeal Court.

The President of the Appeal Court shall issue a decision (ដីកាសម្រេច) to:
- Appoint any Vice-president of the Appeal Court to manage the work on their behalf in case of necessity.
- Appoint a Vice-president of the Appeal Court to be in charge as the president of each chamber according to skills and work experience. In case of a lack of Vice-presidents of the Appeal Court, the President of the Appeal Court may appoint any judge who has a high rank or extensive work experience to be the president of a chamber.
- Define the order for substituting judges in the trial chambers of each chamber in case any judge is absent or has a task.
- Appoint and change court clerks in each chamber according to actual necessity.

### Sub-section 2 (អនុផ្នែកទី ២)
### Jurisdiction (សមត្ថកិច្ច)

**Article 41.- (មាត្រា ៤១.-)**
The Appeal Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate cases within its territorial jurisdiction, except for cases where the law grants jurisdiction to other courts.

**Article 42.- (មាត្រា ៤២.-)**
The Appeal Court decides on both facts (អង្គហេតុ) and law (អង្គច្បាប់) on cases within its jurisdiction in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

**Article 43.- (មាត្រា ៤៣.-)**
The Criminal Chamber has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals against criminal judgments (សាលក្រមព្រហ្មទណ្ឌ) of the First Instance Court and other cases within its jurisdiction by implementing the provisions on criminal procedure in force.

**Article 44.- (មាត្រា ៤៤.-)**
The Civil Chamber has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals against judgments and objections (បណ្តឹងជំទាស់) against decisions of the First Instance Court in civil cases and other cases within its jurisdiction by implementing the provisions on civil procedure in force.

jurisdiction by implementing the provisions on civil procedure in force. The decision shall be made by 03 (three) judges, one of whom is the president.

**Article 45.- (មាត្រា ៤៥.-)**
The Investigation Chamber has the jurisdiction to resolve appeals against investigation acts or decisions (ដីកាសម្រេច) of investigating judges and other cases within its jurisdiction by implementing the provisions on criminal procedure in force. The decision of the Investigation Chamber shall be made by 03 (three) judges, one of whom is the president.

**Article 46.- (មាត្រា ៤៦.-)**
The Commercial Chamber has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals against judgments and objections against decisions of the First Instance Court in commercial cases and other cases within its jurisdiction by implementing the provisions on commercial procedure. The Commercial Chamber of the Appeal Court shall adjudicate by 03 (three) judges, one of whom is the president, accompanied by 02 (two) advisors who are merchants or persons with knowledge of commercial law and who were not commercial advisors in the same case adjudicated by the First Instance Court and the Appeal Court. The verdict (សាលដីកា) of the Commercial Chamber of the Appeal Court shall be made by 03 (three) judges, one of whom is the president, after consulting with the commercial advisors.

Commercial advisors do not fulfill their duties permanently in the Commercial Chamber of the Appeal Court. Commercial advisors shall come to fulfill their duties upon invitation from the President of the Commercial Chamber of the Appeal Court only.

The modalities of appointment and the fulfillment of duties of commercial advisors shall be defined by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice after consulting with the Minister of Commerce.

**Article 47.- (មាត្រា ៤៧.-)**
The Labour Chamber of the Appeal Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals against judgments and objections against decisions of the First Instance Court in labour cases and other cases within its jurisdiction by implementing the provisions on labour procedure. The Labour Chamber of the Appeal Court shall adjudicate by 03 (three) judges, one of whom is the president, accompanied by 02 (two) advisors, one of whom is an employee and the other is an employer, and who were not labour advisors in the same case adjudicated by the First Instance Court and the Appeal Court.

Appeal Court. The decision of the Labour Chamber of the Appeal Court shall be made by 03 (three) judges, one of whom is the president, after consulting with the labour advisors.

Labour advisors do not fulfill their duties permanently in the Labour Chamber of the Appeal Court. Labour advisors shall come to fulfill their duties upon invitation from the President of the Labour Chamber of the Appeal Court only.

The modalities of appointment and the fulfillment of duties of labour advisors shall be defined by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice after consulting with the Minister in charge of the labour sector.

**Article 48.- (មាត្រា ៤៨.-)**
A joint chamber (សភារួមក្រុម) may be established to operate by a decision (ដីកាសម្រេច) of the President of the Appeal Court on their own initiative or upon request from any president of a chamber when any case raises an issue that falls under the jurisdiction of many chambers or if that issue has received conflicting solutions (ដំណោះស្រាយខ្វែងគ្នា) before different chambers of the same Appeal Court. The joint chamber operates upon invitation of the President of the Appeal Court.

 The decision of the joint chamber regarding jurisdiction between various chambers and legal disputes has binding power (អំណាចបង្ខំ) for all chambers of the Appeal Court to follow.

When a joint chamber is established, this chamber must have a composition of at least 05 (five) judges who are equally divided among the judges representing the relevant chambers. The joint chamber is under the presidency of the President of the Appeal Court.

The President of the Appeal Court issues a decision in accordance with the decision of the joint chamber. The decision on jurisdictional disputes and legal disputes is a final decision (សេចក្តីសម្រេចបិទផ្លូវតវ៉ា).

## Section 2 (ផ្នែកទី ២)
## General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court (មហាអយ្យការអមសាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍)

**Article 49.- (មាត្រា ៤៩.-)**
Attached to the Appeal Court, there is a General Prosecution Office (មហាអយ្យការ) which has the following composition:
- Prosecutor General (អគ្គព្រះរាជអាជ្ញា)
- Deputy Prosecutor General (អគ្គព្រះរាជអាជ្ញារង)
- Prosecutor (ព្រះរាជអាជ្ញា)
- Deputy Prosecutor (ព្រះរាជអាជ្ញារង)
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី) and administrative officers (មន្ត្រីរដ្ឋបាល), and may have other legal specialized officers who work at the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court.

administrative officers and may have other legal specialized officers who work at the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court.

**Article 50.- (មាត្រា ៥០.-)**
The functions of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court are entrusted to the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court. Deputy Prosecutors General and Prosecutors attached to the Appeal Court participate in implementing these functions under the leadership and collective responsibility of the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court.

In case of a task, illness, or absence, the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court shall appoint one Deputy Prosecutor General, or if there is no Deputy Prosecutor General, may appoint any Prosecutor to substitute.

In case the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court is in a situation of being unable to work, or in case the position of the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court is vacant, the Minister of Justice shall appoint any Deputy Prosecutor General to serve as the Acting Prosecutor General (អគ្គព្រះរាជអាជ្ញាស្តីទី) instead to ensure the operation of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court until the official appointment of the Prosecutor General.

**Article 51.- (មាត្រា ៥១.-)**
The Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court has management power over Deputy Prosecutors General and Prosecutors attached to the Appeal Court.

The Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court appoints and allocates work to Deputy Prosecutors General and Prosecutors attached to the Appeal Court in various tasks of the General Prosecution Office and the trial chambers.

The conclusions (សេចក្តីសន្នីដ្ឋាន) of the Deputy Prosecutor General or Prosecutor attached to the Appeal Court must be sent to the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court for review before the hearing. If the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court does not agree with that conclusion, and the representative of the General Prosecution Office who makes that conclusion still refuses to comply, the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court may appoint another Deputy Prosecutor General or Prosecutor or appoint themselves to be the representative of the General Prosecution Office in the hearing.

However, during the hearing, the Deputy Prosecutor General or Prosecutor attached to the Appeal Court may freely make oral observations according to what they deem to be in accordance with their conscience. No disciplinary prosecution can be made against the representative of the General Prosecution Office because of their oral observations during the hearing being different from the written conclusions.

The Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court has the right to issue orders (អធិបញ្ជា) to Prosecutors attached to the First Instance Court to prosecute, by implementing the provisions on criminal procedure in force.

## Section 3 (ផ្នែកទី ៣)
## General Secretariat of Administration of the Appeal Court (អគ្គលេខាធិការដ្ឋានរដ្ឋបាលសាលាឧទ្ធរណ៍)

**Article 52.- (មាត្រា ៥២.-)**
The General Secretariat of Administration of the Appeal Court is the chief of staff to the Appeal Court and the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court on:
- Personnel, administrative, and financial work.
- Court administrative management work for technical assistance to the work programs of the Appeal Court and the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court.
- Budget project preparation work for the President of the Appeal Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court to review and decide.
- Implementing budget work according to the approved projects.
- Regularly reporting on personnel, administrative, and financial work to the President of the Appeal Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court.
- Public relations work.
- Periodic submission of verdicts (សាលដីកា) of the Appeal Court to the Ministry of Justice.
- Preparing and submitting monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual personnel, administrative, and financial work reports to the Ministry of Justice.
- Other work assigned by the President of the Appeal Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court.
- Implementing other tasks as defined by legal instruments.

The General Secretariat of Administration of the Appeal Court is divided into departments (នាយកដ្ឋាន) led by one head and several deputy heads as necessary.

The organization and functioning of the General Secretariat of Administration of the Appeal Court shall be defined by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice.

**Article 53.- (មាត្រា ៥៣.-)**
The General Secretariat of Administration of the Appeal Court is led by one Secretary General (អគ្គលេខាធិការ) and several Deputy Secretaries General (អគ្គលេខាធិការរង) as necessary. The Secretary General shall be appointed by Royal Decree upon request reported by the Prime Minister. The Minister of Justice consults with the President of the Appeal Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Appeal Court.

The Secretary General shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 07 (seven) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations.

Deputy Secretaries General and Heads of Departments shall be appointed by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice after consulting with the President of the Appeal Court and the Prosecutor General of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court. Deputy Secretaries General and Heads of Departments shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 05 (five) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations.

The officials working at the General Secretariat below the rank of Head of Department shall be appointed by Prokas (ប្រកាស) of the Minister of Justice. Deputy Heads of Departments as well as Heads and Deputy Heads of offices shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 03 (three) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations.

All officials working at the General Secretariat, including the Secretary General, must have their framework at the Ministry of Justice.

**Article 54.- (មាត្រា ៥៤.-)**
The general assembly (សន្និបាត) of each Appeal Court shall take place under the presidency of the President of the Appeal Court and the Prosecutor General of the General Prosecution Office attached to that Appeal Court to summarize past work results and define the administrative work direction of the Appeal Court for the following year. The general assembly report of the Appeal Court shall be sent to the Ministry of Justice.

# Chapter 4 (ជំពូកទី ៤)
# Supreme Court and General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court (តុលាការកំពូល និងមហាអយ្យការអមតុលាការកំពូល)

## Section 1 (ផ្នែកទី ១)
## Supreme Court (តុលាការកំពូល)

### Sub-section 1 (អនុផ្នែកទី ១)
### Organization and Functioning of the Supreme Court (ការរៀបចំ និងការប្រព្រឹត្តទៅរបស់តុលាការកំពូល)

**Article 55.- (មាត្រា ៥៥.-)**
There is only one Supreme Court, which is located in Phnom Penh.

**Article 56.- (មាត្រា ៥៦.-)**
The composition of the Supreme Court includes:
- President (ប្រធាន)
- Vice-president (អនុប្រធាន)
- Judge (ចៅក្រម)
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី) and administrative officers (មន្ត្រីរដ្ឋបាល), and may have other legal specialized officers who work at the Supreme Court.

**Article 57.- (មាត្រា ៥៧.-)**
The Supreme Court has specialized chambers (សភាជំនាញ) as follows:
- Criminal Chamber (សភាព្រហ្មទណ្ឌ)
- Civil Chamber (សភារដ្ឋប្បវេណី)
- Commercial Chamber (សភាពាណិជ្ជកម្ម)
- Labour Chamber (សភាការងារ).

In case of necessity, other specialized chambers of the Supreme Court may be established by Royal Decree.

Each chamber issues its decisions autonomously in the name of the Supreme Court.

**Article 58.- (មាត្រា ៥៨.-)**
The composition of each chamber includes:
- President of the Chamber (ប្រធានសភា)
- Judge (ចៅក្រម) and
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី).

The president of each chamber is appointed by the President of the Supreme Court. The number of judges, court clerks, and the process of these chambers shall be defined by the President of the Supreme Court.

**Article 59.- (មាត្រា ៥៩.-)**
Each chamber of the Supreme Court adjudicates with 05 (five) judges, one of whom is the president, in accordance with the provisions on procedures in force.

**Article 60.- (មាត្រា ៦០.-)**
The President of the Supreme Court takes necessary management measures for the operation of the Supreme Court and instructs all chambers of the Supreme Court to implement the law.

The President of the Supreme Court shall issue a decision (ដីកាសម្រេច) to:
- Appoint any Vice-president of the Supreme Court to manage the work on their behalf in case of necessity.
- Appoint a Vice-president of the Supreme Court to be in charge as the president of each chamber according to skills and work experience. In case of a lack of Vice-presidents, the President of the Supreme Court may appoint any judge to be the president of a chamber.

### Sub-section 2 (អនុផ្នែកទី ២)
### Jurisdiction (សមត្ថកិច្ច)

**Article 61.- (មាត្រា ៦១.-)**
The Supreme Court has the jurisdiction to resolve cases within its jurisdiction in accordance with the provisions of the law.

**Article 62.- (មាត្រា ៦២.-)**
A plenary chamber (សភាពេញអង្គ) shall be established to operate by a decision of the President of the Supreme Court to adjudicate, inter alia:
- On second appeals (បណ្តឹងសាទុក្ខលើកទីពីរ) against verdicts (សាលដីកា) of the Appeal Court, in accordance with the procedures in force.
- On motions for retrial (បណ្តឹងសើរើ) against final judgments (សាលក្រម) and verdicts, in accordance with the procedures in force.

The plenary chamber may also be established to operate to adjudicate on retrial motions or motions for re-adjudication in case there is a request for review and re-decision on any case from the King who is the President of the Supreme Council of Magistracy (ឧត្តមក្រុមប្រឹក្សានៃអង្គចៅក្រម) through the Minister of Justice.

The plenary chamber operates upon the invitation of the President of the Supreme Court.

The plenary chamber of the Supreme Court is the adjudicating body that issues decisions in the name of the Supreme Court.

When a plenary chamber is established, this chamber must have a composition of at least 09 (nine) judges who have judges representing all chambers of the Supreme Court.

The plenary chamber is under the presidency of the President of the Supreme Court.

**Article 63.- (មាត្រា ៦៣.-)**
A joint chamber (សភារួមក្រុម) may be established to operate by a decision of the President of the Supreme Court on their own initiative or upon request from any president of a chamber when any case raises an issue that falls under the jurisdiction of many chambers or if that issue has received conflicting solutions before different chambers of the Supreme Court. The joint chamber operates upon invitation of the President of the Supreme Court.

The decision of the joint chamber regarding jurisdiction between various chambers and legal disputes has binding power for all chambers of the Supreme Court and lower-level courts to follow.

When a joint chamber is established, this chamber must have a composition of at least 09 (nine) judges who are equally divided among the judges representing the relevant chambers. The joint chamber is under the presidency of the President of the Supreme Court.

The President of the Supreme Court issues a decision in accordance with the decision of the joint chamber. The decision on jurisdictional disputes and legal disputes is a final decision (សេចក្តីសម្រេចបិទផ្លូវតវ៉ា).

**Article 64.- (មាត្រា ៦៤.-)**
The Criminal Chamber of the Supreme Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals (បណ្តឹងសាទុក្ខ) against criminal verdicts of the Appeal Court by implementing the provisions on criminal procedure in force.

**Article 65.- (មាត្រា ៦៥.-)**
The Civil Chamber of the Supreme Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals against verdicts and objections against decisions in civil matters of the Appeal Court, as well as on appeals against civil judgments of the First Instance Court and other cases by implementing the provisions on civil procedure in force.

**Article 66.- (មាត្រា ៦៦.-)**
The Commercial Chamber of the Supreme Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals against verdicts and objections against decisions in commercial matters of the Appeal Court by implementing the provisions on commercial procedure.

**Article 67.- (មាត្រា ៦៧.-)**
The Labour Chamber of the Supreme Court has the jurisdiction to adjudicate on appeals against verdicts and objections against decisions in labour matters of the Appeal Court by implementing the provisions on labour procedure.

## Section 2 (ផ្នែកទី ២)
## General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court (មហាអយ្យការអមតុលាការកំពូល)

**Article 68.- (មាត្រា ៦៨.-)**
The composition of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court includes:
- Prosecutor General (អគ្គព្រះរាជអាជ្ញា)
- Deputy Prosecutor General (អគ្គព្រះរាជអាជ្ញារង)
- Prosecutor (ព្រះរាជអាជ្ញា)
- Court clerk (ក្រឡាបញ្ជី) and administrative officers (មន្ត្រីរដ្ឋបាល), and may have other legal specialized officers who work at the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court.

**Article 69.- (មាត្រា ៦៩.-)**
The functions of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court are entrusted to the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court. Deputy Prosecutors General and Prosecutors attached to the Supreme Court participate in implementing these functions under the leadership and collective responsibility of the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court.

In case of a task, illness, or absence, the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court shall appoint one Deputy Prosecutor General, or if there is no Deputy Prosecutor General, may appoint any Prosecutor to substitute.

In case the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court is in a situation of being unable to work, or in case the position of the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court is vacant, the Minister of Justice shall appoint any Deputy Prosecutor General to serve as the Acting Prosecutor General (អគ្គព្រះរាជអាជ្ញាស្តីទី) instead to ensure the operation of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court until the official appointment of the Prosecutor General.

**Article 70.- (មាត្រា ៧០.-)**
The Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court has management power over Deputy Prosecutors General and Prosecutors attached to the Supreme Court. The Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court appoints and allocates work to Deputy Prosecutors General and Prosecutors attached to the Supreme Court in various tasks of the General Prosecution Office and in the trial chambers.

The conclusions (សេចក្តីសន្នីដ្ឋាន) of the Deputy Prosecutor General or Prosecutor attached to the Supreme Court must be sent to the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court for review before the hearing. If the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court does not agree with that conclusion, and the representative of the General Prosecution Office who makes that conclusion still refuses to comply, the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court may appoint another Deputy Prosecutor General or Prosecutor or appoint themselves to be the representative of the General Prosecution Office in the hearing.

However, during the hearing, the Deputy Prosecutor General or Prosecutor attached to the Supreme Court may freely make oral observations according to what they deem to be in accordance with their conscience. No disciplinary prosecution can be made against the representative of the General Prosecution Office because of their oral observations during the hearing being different from the written conclusions.

## Section 3 (ផ្នែកទី ៣)
## General Secretariat of Administration of the Supreme Court (អគ្គលេខាធិការដ្ឋានរដ្ឋបាលតុលាការកំពូល)

**Article 71.- (មាត្រា ៧១.-)**
The General Secretariat of Administration of the Supreme Court is the chief of staff to the Supreme Court and the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court on:
- Personnel, administrative, and financial work.
- Court administrative management work for technical assistance to the work programs of the Court.
- Budget project preparation work for the President of the Supreme Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court to review and decide.
- Regularly reporting on personnel, administrative, and financial work to the President of the Supreme Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court.
- Public relations work.
- Periodic submission of verdicts (សាលដីកា) of the Supreme Court to the Ministry of Justice.
- Preparing and submitting monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual personnel, administrative, and financial work reports to the Ministry of Justice.
- Implementing budget work according to the approved projects.
- Other work assigned by the President of the Supreme Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court.
- Implementing other tasks as defined by legal instruments.

Other work assigned by the President of the Supreme Court and the Prosecutor General attached to the Supreme Court.
- Implementing other tasks as defined by legal instruments.

The General Secretariat of Administration of the Supreme Court is divided into departments led by one head and several deputy heads as necessary.

The organization and functioning of the General Secretariat of Administration of the Supreme Court shall be defined by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice.

**Article 72.- (មាត្រា ៧២.-)**
The General Secretariat of Administration of the Supreme Court is led by one Secretary General and several Deputy Secretaries General as necessary.

The Secretary General shall be appointed by Royal Decree upon request from the Prime Minister. The Minister of Justice consults with the President of the Supreme Court and the Prosecutor General of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court to submit a request to the Prime Minister. The Secretary General shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 07 (seven) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations.

Deputy Secretaries General and Heads of Departments shall be appointed by Sub-decree upon request from the Minister of Justice after consulting with the President of the Supreme Court and the Prosecutor General of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court. Deputy Secretaries General and Heads of Departments shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 05 (five) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations.

The officials working at the General Secretariat below the rank of Head of Department shall be appointed by Prokas (ប្រកាស) of the Minister of Justice. Deputy Heads of Departments as well as Heads and Deputy Heads of offices shall be selected from civil servants who have at least 03 (three) years of work experience in legal, administrative, or financial specializations.

All officials working at the General Secretariat, including the Secretary General, must have their framework at the Ministry of Justice.

**Article 73.- (មាត្រា ៧៣.-)**
The general assembly (សន្និបាត) of the Supreme Court shall take place under the presidency of the President of the Supreme Court and the Prosecutor General of the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court to summarize past work results and define the administrative work direction of the Supreme Court for the following year. The general assembly report of the Supreme Court shall be sent to the Ministry of Justice.

# Chapter 5 (ជំពូកទី ៥)
# Incompatibility (វិសមិតភាព)

**Article 74.- (មាត្រា ៧៤.-)**
The functions of prosecution, investigation, and adjudication must be separated from each other. Any judge who has already been in charge of handling any case in the capacity of a representative of the prosecution or as an investigating judge cannot adjudicate or participate in adjudicating that case which they handled; otherwise, the judgment or verdict shall be null and void.

**Article 75.- (មាត្រា ៧៥.-)**
A judge cannot participate in adjudicating the same case together with one or more judges who are spouses (សហព័ទ្ធ) or blood relatives (ញាតិលោហិត) up to the 4th (fourth) degree, including this 4th (fourth) degree, or relatives by marriage (ញាតិពន្ធ) up to the 3rd (third) degree, including this 3rd (third) degree, whether in the capacity of an adjudicating judge or a representative of the prosecution. This principle shall also be applied to judges in higher courts for cases adjudicated by judges in lower courts who are spouses or blood relatives up to the 4th (fourth) degree, including this 4th (fourth) degree, or relatives by marriage up to the 3rd (third) degree, including this 3rd (third) degree.

**Article 76.- (មាត្រា ៧៦.-)**
All judges who have spouses or blood relatives up to the 4th (fourth) degree, including this 4th (fourth) degree, or relatives by marriage up to the 3rd (third) degree, including this 3rd (third) degree, serving as a lawyer for any party in any case cannot participate in adjudicating that case.

**Article 77.- (មាត្រា ៧៧.-)**
A judge cannot participate in adjudicating any case where one party is a spouse or blood relative up to the 6th (sixth) degree, including this 6th (sixth) degree, or relative by marriage up to the 3rd (third) degree, including this 3rd (third) degree.

**Article 78.- (មាត្រា ៧៨.-)**
Unless there are provisions on procedures stating otherwise, all parties in a case and persons who have an interest in a case, including the representative of the prosecution, can file a motion for nullity (ប្តឹងសុំមោឃកម្ម) against a judgment or verdict of a court due to a violation of the rules on incompatibility as stated in Article 74, Article 75, Article 76, and Article 77 above.

This motion for nullity can be made at any time before the court in the recourse procedure (នីតិវិធីឧបាស្រ័យ) by implementing the provisions on procedures in force. Even if that judgment or verdict has become final (ស្ថាពរ), the motion for nullity can still be made within 60 (sixty) days from the date of knowing about the grounds stated in Article 74, Article 75, Article 76, and Article 77 above after the judgment or verdict has become final. In the latter case, the motion for nullity must be filed at the court that issued the final judgment or verdict, but there must be a different composition of adjudicating judges to review and decide on the nullity of that final judgment or verdict and to implement further procedures in accordance with the provisions in force.

# Chapter 6 (ជំពូកទី ៦)
# Budgets of Courts and Prosecution Offices attached to Courts (ថវិកាសាលាជម្រះក្តី និងអយ្យការអមសាលាជម្រះក្តី)

**Article 79.- (មាត្រា ៧៩.-)**
The First Instance Court and the Prosecution Office attached to the First Instance Court, the Appeal Court and the General Prosecution Office attached to the Appeal Court, as well as the Supreme Court and the General Prosecution Office attached to the Supreme Court, have separate budget packages for operation, which are located within the budget package of the Ministry of Justice.

The President of the court at all levels is an orderer (អាណាប័ក) delegated by the Minister of Justice.

The management and allocation of the budgets of courts and prosecution offices attached to courts as defined in the 1st paragraph above shall be defined by Sub-decree.

# Chapter 7 (ជំពូកទី ៧)
# Inter-provisions (អន្តរប្បញ្ញត្តិ)

**Article 80.- (មាត្រា ៨០.-)**
Courts at all levels as well as prosecution organizations attached to these courts which were established before this law enters into force shall continue their operation in accordance with the provisions of this law.

**Article 81.- (មាត្រា ៨១.-)**
Previous provisions related to the Military Court and the Prosecution Office attached to the Military Court, as well as provisions on jurisdiction and procedure applied for the processing of military offense cases, shall continue to have the force of implementation after this law enters into force until there are new provisions to replace them.

**Article 82.- (មាត្រា ៨២.-)**
While waiting for the putting into operation of other Appeal Courts, the current Appeal Court located in Phnom Penh has territorial jurisdiction extending over the entire territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

**Article 83.- (មាត្រា ៨៣.-)**
The putting into operation of various specialized courts of the First Instance Court as stated in Article 14 of this law shall be done by Prokas of the Minister of Justice.

**Article 84.- (មាត្រា ៨៤.-)**
In case the First Instance Court of any province has not yet been put into operation or cannot be put into operation, the jurisdiction to adjudicate all cases in that province shall be granted to any First Instance Court by Royal Decree.

**Article 85.- (មាត្រា ៨៥.-)**
When the Commercial Chamber and the Labour Chamber of the higher courts (សាលាជម្រះក្តីជាន់ខ្ពស់) cannot operate due to a lack of judges, the adjudication of commercial cases and labour cases is the jurisdiction of the Civil Chamber of the higher courts. These tasks shall be managed by the President of the higher court where the specialized chamber is located.

When any specialized chamber above operates in accordance with this law, other specialized chambers must transfer cases that are not within their jurisdiction and have not yet been handled back to the specialized chamber that has jurisdiction.

**Article 86.- (មាត្រា ៨៦.-)**
In case there are not yet enough judges, an investigating judge can continue to fulfill the function as an adjudicating judge, but cannot adjudicate a case which they investigated.

**Article 87.- (មាត្រា ៨៧.-)**
In case there is not yet an administrative court, the jurisdiction to adjudicate administrative cases shall be granted to the civil courts of the lower courts (សាលាជម្រះក្តីជាន់ទាប) and the Civil Chamber of the higher courts.

**Article 88.- (មាត្រា ៨៨.-)**
When there are not yet commercial advisors or labour advisors, the composition for adjudicating commercial cases and labour cases shall implement the provisions on civil procedure.

**Article 89.- (មាត្រា ៨៩.-)**
When there are not yet provisions on commercial procedure, the adjudication of commercial cases shall implement the provisions on civil procedure and other legal provisions in force.

When there are not yet provisions on labour procedure, the adjudication of labour cases shall implement the provisions on civil procedure and other legal provisions in force.

When there are not yet provisions on administrative procedure, the adjudication of administrative cases shall implement the provisions on civil procedure and other legal provisions in force.

**Article 90.- (មាត្រា ៩០.-)**
In the first 05 (five) years after this law enters into force, the appointment of heads of administrative units of courts at all levels can be implemented according to actual qualification conditions.

 The Director of Clerks (នាយកក្រឡាបញ្ជី) of the First Instance Court can be appointed as the head or deputy head of the Administrative Secretariat of the First Instance Court where they are currently working.

The Director of Clerks of the higher courts can be appointed as the Secretary General or Deputy Secretary General of the General Secretariat of Administration of the higher courts where they are currently working.

# Chapter 8 (ជំពូកទី ៨)
# Final Provisions (អវសានប្បញ្ញត្តិ)

**Article 91.- (មាត្រា ៩១.-)**
Provisions on the judicial system, criminal law, and criminal procedure for implementation in Cambodia during the transitional period dated September 10, 1992, and the Law on the Organization and Activities of the Courts of the State of Cambodia promulgated by Decree No. 06 Kr dated February 08, 1993, as well as any provisions contrary to this law, shall be nullified and replaced by this law.

Nation Religion King

# Law on Peaceful Demonstration

2009

Contents

# Contents

# Law on Peaceful Demonstration

( Contains 6 Chapters and 30 Articles )

Royal Decree No. NS/RKM/1209/025 Promulgating the Law on Peaceful Demonstration

- Chapter 1: General Provisions (Article 1 to Article 4)

- Chapter 2: Procedures for Notification of Peaceful Demonstration (Article 5 to Article 14)

- Chapter 3: Responsibilities of Demonstration Leaders and Competent Authorities (Article 15 to Article 20)

- Chapter 4: Procedures for Resolving Offenses and Penal Provisions (Article 21 to Article 27)

- Chapter 5: Transitional Provisions (Article 28)

- Chapter 6: Final Provisions (Article 29 to Article 30)

Royal Decree

NS/RKM/1209/025

We

His Majesty King Norodom Sihamoni, United Nation, Religion, King, and the King who is loyal to the Khmer people, the Great King who protects the Khmer people, the King of the Independent State of Cambodia, the sovereign king of peace, prosperity, and happiness for the Khmer people.

- Having seen the Constitution of the Kingdom of Cambodia

- Having seen the Royal Decree No. NS/RKT/0908/1055 dated September 25, 2008, on the Appointment of the Royal Government of the Kingdom of Cambodia

- Having seen the Royal Code No. 02/NS/94 dated July 20, 1994, promulgating the Law on the Organization and Functioning of the Council of Ministers

- Having seen the Royal Code No. NS/RKM/0196/08 dated January 24, 1996, promulgating the Law on the Establishment of the Ministry of Interior

- Having seen the Request of Samdech Akka Moha Sena Padei Techo Hun Sen, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Cambodia, and the Minister of Interior

#### Promulgate

The Law on Peaceful Demonstration, which was adopted by the National Assembly on October 21, 2009, during the 3rd plenary session of the 4th legislature, and which was approved in its entirety by the Senate without any amendment on November 17, 2009, during the 6th plenary session of the 2nd legislature, the full text of which is as follows:

# Law on Peaceful Demonstration

## Chapter 1
## General Provisions

#### Article 1._
This law aims to determine the organization and functioning of peaceful demonstration in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

#### Article 2._
This law aims to ensure the protection of the freedom of expression of Cambodian citizens through peaceful demonstration, but this right shall not be abused to affect the rights, freedoms and honors of others, good customs of the national society, public order and national security.

#### Article 3._
This law has the scope of application to all gatherings or marches for peaceful demonstration in the Kingdom of Cambodia, but does not apply to:

1- Meetings or gatherings or marches in any election campaign.

2- Gatherings inside and outside the fences of factories or enterprises or various institutions related to labor disputes which shall be included in the scope of the Labor Law.

3- Marches, parades, funeral processions and other gatherings for the purpose of serving religion, arts, culture, national tradition and educational dissemination activities for social benefits.

#### Article 4._
Peaceful demonstration refers to the gathering or march by a group of people to demand, protest or publicly express sentiments, ideas or their will peacefully or by other peaceful means.

## Chapter 2
## Procedures for Notification of Peaceful Demonstration

#### Article 5._
Any group of people intending to organize a peaceful demonstration in any public place shall notify in writing to the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province managing that place.

#### Article 6._
The notification shall specify:

- Surname, given name and permanent address for communication of three (3) leaders, with copies of Cambodian national identity cards attached.

- Purpose of the peaceful demonstration.

- Date, time and duration of the peaceful demonstration, the place and routes to be used for activities, the number of participants, as well as the number of vehicles by each type.

All notification applicants shall ensure to respect and fulfill their roles and responsibilities as stated in Article 16 of this law.

#### Article 7._
The notification shall be submitted to the Capital Hall or Provincial Hall at least five (5) working days prior to the scheduled date of the peaceful demonstration.

#### Article 8._
Upon receiving the notification, the Capital Hall or Provincial Hall:

1- Issue a written receipt to the person who submitted the notification.

2- Disseminate this notification immediately in an easily visible place in the administrative building or on its official website.

3- Send copies of this notification to the local police commissioner, the Royal Gendarmerie office, and other relevant competent authorities involved in the demonstration site.

#### Article 9._
The competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province shall respond positively to the notification in writing, except when:

- The peaceful demonstration is held on the days of the King's Birthday Ceremony, the King's Coronation Ceremony, the Water Festival, the Moon Salutation and Ak Ambok, the National Independence Day, the Khmer Traditional New Year, and the Pchum Ben Festival.

- There is clear information that the demonstration will cause any danger or will seriously affect security, safety and public order.

#### Article 10._
The competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province shall examine and respond within a maximum of three (3) working days from the date the notification was submitted. If the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province fail to respond by the scheduled time of the peaceful demonstration, it means the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province have agreed.

#### Article 11._
In case the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province have clear information that...

this peaceful demonstration will cause any danger or will seriously affect security, safety and public order, the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province shall respond by immediately notifying the applicant so that they can meet with the local authorities and other relevant authorities to consider and discuss for a resolution.

#### Article 12._
After the discussion, if both parties still cannot reach an agreement, the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province shall request a decision from the Minister of Interior.

#### Article 13._
The decision of the Minister of Interior shall be made in writing and shall be provided to the applicant at least twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled time of the peaceful demonstration. Copies of the decision, including details of the agreed amendments, shall be provided to the relevant competent authorities and to other authorities whose areas might be affected by this peaceful demonstration.

#### Article 14._
The full specification and guarantee as stated in paragraph 1 of Article 6 of this Law are not required, only a written notification signed or thumbprinted and accompanied by copies of Cambodian national identity cards of three (3) leaders to the local competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province at least twelve (12) hours during working days or thirty-six (36) hours during holidays before the peaceful demonstration, if the peaceful demonstration is held at the following places:

1- At public expression places established legally according to laws or regulations, and where the peaceful demonstration has a maximum of two hundred (200) participants for each Capital or Province.

2- At private property or collective property with the consent of the owner or the management committee responsible for that collective property, and the peaceful demonstration has a maximum of two hundred (200) participants.

However, in case there are two (2) or more different groups wishing to hold a peaceful demonstration at the same place and time, the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province shall decide that the group who submitted the notification first shall have the priority, or may allow the other group to hold it at another place at least five hundred (500) meters away.

The peaceful demonstration as stated in this article can only take place between 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM only.

## Chapter 3
## Responsibilities of Demonstration Leaders and Competent Authorities

#### Article 15._
For a peaceful demonstration that has been agreed upon and involves a march on public roads, the territorial authorities of the Commune, Sangkat, District, Khan, Municipality, Province, Capital, or officials appointed as representatives shall cooperate with the local police and the Royal Gendarmerie to prevent any possible bad consequences by determining the aforementioned routes to facilitate and ease traffic for vehicles to avoid serious disruption to work processes, businesses, services, commerce, or other trades.

#### Article 16._
Leaders of a peaceful demonstration shall be responsible for taking appropriate measures to ensure that the demonstration will take place peacefully and according to the following conditions:

1- Notify the participants about their responsibilities as stated in point 3 of this Article.

2- Discuss and cooperate with local officials and relevant competent authorities to ensure the demonstration takes place peacefully.

3- Maintain order and good discipline correctly according to the scheduled time and place from the start to the end of the peaceful demonstration.

#### Article 17._
The competent authorities shall take measures to protect the spirit of peaceful demonstration to ensure security, safety and public order are well maintained and shall not interfere with the process of the peaceful demonstration.

#### Article 18._
When there is a request for assistance from the leaders of a peaceful demonstration, the competent authorities shall make efforts to carefully respond to reasonable requests based on law to ensure the exercise of the right to peaceful demonstration and the exercise of the right to freedom of public expression with dignity.

#### Article 19._
Competent authorities appointed to maintain security, safety and public order at peaceful demonstration sites shall wear proper uniforms, including name tags and identification numbers displayed on the front, and must strictly maintain dignified behavior.

#### Article 20._
Peaceful demonstrations that have been agreed upon, including cases where the competent territorial authorities of the Capital or Province failed to respond as stated in Article 10 of this Law, shall not be dispersed.

In case a peaceful demonstration becomes violent, the competent authorities shall take appropriate measures to prevent and stop this demonstration immediately.

Even if a demonstration is conducted peacefully, if no notification was submitted according to Article 5, Article 6 and Article 14 of this Law, the competent authorities may take measures to stop that demonstration.

## Chapter 4
## Procedures for Resolving Offenses and Penal Provisions

#### Article 21._
A written warning shall be issued to the leaders of a peaceful demonstration who have violated Article 5, Article 16 and Article 20, paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Law.

#### Article 22._
A written warning shall be issued to any territorial authority official or competent authority official who has violated Article 17, Article 18, Article 19 and Article 20, paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Law.

#### Article 23._
In case any demonstration involves carrying instruments that could cause danger or affect others, or committed any act that interferes with the rights and freedoms of others, the competent authorities shall seize those instruments or prohibit such acts from continuing. If those individuals are stubborn and refuse to hand over...

give it up or refuse to stop committing such acts, the competent authorities shall temporarily detain them until the peaceful demonstration is completely finished, then they will be released, unless there is any other offense.

#### Article 24._
In case any demonstrator carries weapons or explosives, the competent authorities shall seize those weapons or explosives and detain them, then send them to the competent institutions for resolution according to the laws in force.

#### Article 25._
Any person who takes the opportunity during a peaceful demonstration to commit theft, robbery or cause damage to private property or public property shall be punished according to the criminal law in force.

#### Article 26._
If the process of the peaceful demonstration causes violence resulting in damage to private property or public property, the repair of the damage shall be the responsibility of the perpetrator and the accomplice.

In case those individuals do not have the ability to repair the damage, the competent authorities shall compile a case file and send it to the court.

#### Article 27._
If the process of the peaceful demonstration causes violence, any person who commits an offense resulting in injury or death to competent authorities or demonstrators or other persons shall be punished according to the criminal law in force.

## Chapter 5
## Transitional Provisions

#### Article 28._
Within six (6) months after this Law enters into force, each Capital and Province shall create a "Public Expression Place" by choosing a suitable open space or center with high safety, and where it is easy to hear and see within its jurisdiction for peaceful demonstrations or public expression as stated in Article 14 of this Law.

## Chapter 6
## Final Provisions

#### Article 29._
The Law on Demonstration adopted by the National Assembly of the State of Cambodia on December 27, 1991, promulgated by Decree No. 114 Kr. dated December 28, 1991, and any provisions contrary to this Law shall be null and void.

#### Article 30._
This Law shall be declared as urgent.
